pairs.subject: agent-browser-control
pairs.evidence: crates/table-client/src/authority_table.rs:228 The one browser-named command is a privileged approval-window wallet decision that hands a link to the system browser, and searching crates/table-client for puppeteer, chromium, websocket, locator, daemon and webdriver found nothing, so this IPC contract is not an agent browser-control surface.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-client/src/authority_table.rs:1 This single-source command table classes window IPC commands by tier and label. It does not cover browser commands, so the technique's precondition does not hold, although its shape is similar.
crates/table-client/src/authority.rs:290 Admission here is keyed by Tauri window label, such as devtools being refused. No browser daemon listener is exposed to remote agents.
crates/table-client/src/lib.rs:330 The command returns unit after handing a link to the system browser. No browser process is kept alive or addressed.
